title: Week Ahead — Market Outlook
headline: Markets enter September with contained but rising event risk as sticky inflation and hawkish Fed repricing meet a jobs-heavy calendar, Treasury supply and another high-stakes AI earnings test.
volatilityRationale: Markets are walking into multiple volatility triggers—JOLTS, manufacturing data, the Beige Book, Fed speeches, Treasury bill auctions, Broadcom earnings and Friday’s employment report—but the VIX remains around 15 rather than signaling a panic regime. The main risk is a fast repricing in rates and long-duration technology if inflation, labor data or Fed communication challenge hopes for easier policy.

recap.text: Large-cap U.S. benchmarks finished the August 24–28 week higher, while small caps lagged; Friday’s session faded as bond yields rose and rate-hike bets strengthened.
July PCE inflation came in hotter than expected, keeping the inflation-versus-growth trade at the center of equity and Treasury pricing ahead of the Fed’s Jackson Hole messaging.
Nvidia’s earnings and outlook beat expectations and briefly revived AI-risk appetite, with shares and the technology complex rallying into Thursday’s session.

Fed Chair Kevin Warsh’s Jackson Hole comments pushed investors toward higher near-term rate expectations; stocks dipped Friday as yields rose, leaving duration-sensitive technology exposed to further repricing.
Iran-related sanctions and Middle East uncertainty kept oil and geopolitical risk in the market narrative, with the potential to reappear as an inflation or risk-premium shock.

triggers.text: Job Openings and Labor Turnover Survey for July is scheduled for 10:00 a.m. ET, providing an early read on labor-market cooling before Friday’s payrolls report.
ISM Manufacturing PMI is due at 10:00 a.m. ET, while Fed Governor Michael Barr is scheduled to speak at 9:05 a.m. ET on the economic outlook and financial inclusion.
The Treasury’s tentative schedule lists 6-week and 52-week bill auctions, making front-end supply and rate sensitivity an additional market check.

The Federal Reserve’s Beige Book is scheduled for 2:00 p.m. ET; Broadcom is also scheduled to report fiscal Q3 results after the close, putting AI-semiconductor demand and hyperscaler spending back in focus.
Productivity and Costs (revision) is due at 8:30 a.m. ET and Fed Governor Christopher Waller is scheduled to discuss the economic outlook at 8:30 a.m. ET; both could influence the rates narrative.
The August Employment Situation is scheduled for 8:30 a.m. ET, the week’s clearest test of whether labor-market conditions are cooling enough to change policy expectations.

watch.text: VIX is around 15.2, above Friday’s 14.43 close but still below the levels normally associated with acute equity stress; watch whether a move higher confirms the week’s event risk rather than remaining a contained-volatility blip.
Monitor CBOE SKEW alongside VIX for tail-risk pricing; no fresh SKEW value was used here, so the signal should be treated as a live check rather than a fixed reading.

Rates are the main cross-asset transmission channel: sticky inflation and hawkish Fed communication can pressure long-duration technology, while softer labor data could revive easing expectations and support growth multiples.

AI-capex breadth is back on the tape with Broadcom’s report; watch whether custom silicon, networking and hyperscaler commentary validate the Nvidia-led rally or expose concentration risk in semiconductors.
